# Oklahoma in the SEC: Two Seasons In (2024-25 and 2025-26)

*Data as of October 2026; the 2026-27 season is in progress and not included. Every figure here is regenerated by `ou-sec all`. `tests/test_reports_in_sync.py` fails if the committed tables, or the key figures quoted below, drift from the code. A readable version of this report is the story page, `docs/index.html`.*

## Executive summary

- **OU wins fewer conference titles in the SEC: 1.5 a year, against 2.40 in its last five Big 12 years.** In the seven sports it plays in both leagues, OU won 3 SEC titles in 2 years. Its recent Big 12 pace implied 4.80.
- **Texas, which moved the same day from the same starting point, held steady.** Texas averaged 2.40 titles a year in its last five Big 12 years and 2.50 in the SEC (5 titles). This is the most informative comparison in the project, because it holds the conference change constant.
- **Neither gap is statistically meaningful yet.** If OU had kept its recent Big 12 rate, a shortfall this size would happen about 29% of the time (p = 0.29). If OU and Texas were equally strong in the SEC, a 3-to-5 split or worse would happen about 36% of the time (p = 0.36). Two of OU's SEC outcomes are unknown (women's soccer tournaments). Counting them as titles only raises those p-values, to 0.65 and 0.62.
- **Gymnastics shows the SEC's depth best.** OU won 15 Big 12 meet titles and won the NCAA title in both SEC years, yet lost both SEC Championship meets: by 0.275 to LSU and by 0.025 to Florida.
- **Nationally, OU is as strong as ever.** It won 3 national titles in 2 SEC years (gymnastics twice and baseball in 2026) and finished 9th and 16th in the Directors' Cup. Oklahoma State, still in the Big 12, finished 29th and 28th. Texas finished 1st both years.
- **Bottom line (my judgment, moderate confidence):** OU has kept its national standing but is converting it into fewer conference trophies, and is doing so worse than Texas. Two seasons cannot tell a real decline apart from a run of close losses. The 2026-27 and 2027-28 seasons will decide it.

## 1. Data and method

| Layer | Source | Coverage | Trust |
|---|---|---|---|
| Big 12 history | `data/raw/big12_champions/` (scraped from Wikipedia) and `data/curated/big12_supplement.csv` (2023-24, curated with sources) | 13 sports, 1995-96 to 2023-24 | Medium (scrape) / high (supplement) |
| SEC era | `data/curated/sec_results.csv`, one sourced row per school, sport and season | OU and Texas, 2024-25 and 2025-26 (30 rows) | Tagged per row: 19 high, 10 medium, 1 low |
| National context | `data/curated/directors_cup.csv` | OU, Texas, Oklahoma State | High/medium |

The build environment could not reach Wikipedia directly, so every curated row came from web-search results, cross-checked against a second source where possible. Conflicts are recorded in each row's `notes`. Full rules are in `docs/METHODOLOGY.md` and `docs/DATA_DICTIONARY.md`.

**Comparable basket.** Only sports and title types that exist in both leagues count: baseball, softball, men's and women's basketball, women's soccer (regular season + tournament), volleyball (regular season), and women's gymnastics (championship meet). Texas has no gymnastics program, so its basket has six sports. Each school is compared with its *own* history in the same sports.

## 2. Big 12 baseline

OU ranks **2nd** of 16 schools in all-time Big 12 titles in these records with 64 (11.7%), behind Texas (140). The total includes spring 1996, when the Big 12 held a softball season a year before other sports began. OU won both titles that year.

| Sport | Reg. season | Tournament/Meet | Total |
|---|---|---|---|
| Softball | 15 | 9 | 24 |
| Women's Gymnastics | — | 15 | 15 |
| Women's Basketball | 6 | 4 | 10 |
| Men's Tennis | 2 | 3 | 5 |
| Baseball | 1 | 3 | 4 |
| Men's Basketball / Wrestling | 0 | 3 each | 3 each |

In the comparable basket OU averaged **1.93** titles a year over 28 full Big 12 years and **2.40** over its last five, with 4 in its final season.

## 3. SEC era, sport by sport (Oklahoma)

| Sport | 2024-25 | 2025-26 | SEC titles | National |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Football | 2-6, Armed Forces Bowl L | 6-2, CFP first round L | 0 | — |
| Softball | 17-7, **reg. season champ**, **tourney co-champ**, WCWS | 20-4, **reg. season champ**, Super Regional L | 3 | — |
| W Gymnastics | 7-1, **reg. season co-champ**, 2nd at SEC meet | 8-0, **outright reg. season**, 2nd at SEC meet | 2 (reg. season, outside basket) | **NCAA ×2** |
| Baseball | 14-16, regional final L | 14-16, lost SEC opener | 0 | **2026 NCAA** |
| W Basketball | 11-5, Sweet 16 | 11-5, Sweet 16 | 0 | — |
| M Basketball | 6-12, NCAA first round | 7-11, missed NCAA | 0 | — |
| Volleyball | 8-8, NCAA second round | 7-8 | 0 | — |
| W Soccer | record and tournament *unknown* | 3-4-3; tournament *unknown* | 0 (2 unknown) | — |

**Texas for comparison:** baseball won the 2025 SEC regular season, softball won the 2026 SEC tournament and both national titles, women's basketball shared the 2025 regular season and won the 2026 tournament, and soccer won the 2024 tournament. Football reached the 2024 SEC title game.

## 4. Statistics

| School | Baseline | Rate/yr | Expected in 2 SEC yrs | Observed | P(≤ observed) | P if unknowns were titles |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Oklahoma | Big 12 full history | 1.93 | 3.86 | 3 | 0.46 | 0.81 |
| Oklahoma | Big 12 last 5 years | 2.40 | 4.80 | 3 | 0.29 | 0.65 |
| Texas | Big 12 full history | 1.75 | 3.50 | 5 | 0.86 | 0.86 |
| Texas | Big 12 last 5 years | 2.40 | 4.80 | 5 | 0.65 | 0.65 |

**OU vs Texas, exact conditional test:** given 8 combined SEC titles and equal expected rates, OU's share follows Binomial(8, 0.5). P(OU ≤ 3) = 0.36, or 0.62 if OU's two unknowns were titles.

- **ELI5:** OU won one or two fewer titles than usual and Texas didn't. Coin flips go that way often enough that two seasons can't prove anything.
- **Intermediate:** At p ≈ 0.3 neither result is close to the usual 0.05 threshold. For the OU-vs-Texas gap to reach it, OU would have needed 0 titles against Texas's 5, or 1 against 7 or more.
- **Advanced:** Both tests assume titles are independent Poisson events at a constant rate. Titles cluster within a sport (softball's regular-season and tournament titles are correlated), which inflates variance and makes these p-values *too small*, if anything. The SEC's depth should also lower the true rate for everyone. The Texas comparison absorbs that shared conference effect, which is why it is the better test.
- **Expert:** The design is a two-unit, two-period difference-in-differences with count outcomes. The natural next model is a Poisson GLM, titles ~ school × era with log-exposure (sports in basket), or better, a continuous outcome: conference finish percentile per sport-season with sport fixed effects. That needs final standings, not title lists. See `docs/ROADMAP.md`.

## 5. Limitations

- **Small n.** Two SEC seasons, two schools.
- **Search-sourced SEC data.** 10 of 30 rows are medium confidence and 1 is low. Notable conflicts: OU men's basketball 2025-26 (19-15 vs 21-16), and Texas's 2024 volleyball finish (single source).
- **Shared Big 12 titles may be undercounted** before 2023-24. The scraped tables list one name for some co-championships. One example found: 1996 softball's regular season was likely shared with Oklahoma State, which the scraped row omits.
- **Volleyball and gymnastics titles mean different things in each league.** The SEC re-launched a volleyball tournament in 2025, and SEC gymnastics added a regular-season title. Both are excluded from the comparable basket.
- **Basket differs by school** (7 sports for OU, 6 for Texas). Each school is measured against its own baseline in its own basket, so the comparison is rates against rates, not raw counts.

## 6. Next steps

See `docs/ROADMAP.md`. The top item: replace title counts with conference finish percentile, built from final standings, for a model that can detect real change within three or four seasons instead of six or more.
